data_description.scan_interval:
How often power, energy and the meter's status are read, in seconds: anything from 0.01 to 300, such as 2 or 0.5. The default is 2. Use 1 or less for something like battery control.

Reading the default sensors takes about 0.42 s at 9600 baud, 0.19 s at 38400 and 0.16 s at 57600. A shorter interval than that does not make updates faster; if yours is shorter, you are warned after selecting Submit.

serial_baudrate.description:
The meter at Modbus address {unit_id} answered at **{baudrate} baud**, so that rate is filled in below.

A meter keeps its baud rate in its own settings, and those can only be read once Home Assistant talks to it at that rate. So it tried each rate the meters offer (9600, 19200, 38400, 57600 and 115200) until the meter answered. Change it only if you know the meter is set to another rate.

serial_not_found.description:
No meter answered at Modbus address {unit_id} at any of the baud rates the meters offer (9600, 19200, 38400, 57600 and 115200).

A meter keeps its baud rate in its own settings, and those can only be read once Home Assistant talks to it at that rate, so it tried each one. Check the wiring first: swapping A and B is worth a try.

If the meter's Modbus address was changed, Home Assistant can search every address at every rate, which takes up to about 6 minutes. Or enter the baud rate the meter shows in its setup menu yourself.

interval_warning.title: Short update interval
interval_warning.description:
You set the readings to update every {interval}, but a poll of the meter takes {poll} at {baudrate} baud.

- Updates will not come faster than a poll takes. Home Assistant starts the interval when a poll ends, so the meter is read without pause, and other devices on the same bus wait longer for their turn.
- Home Assistant records a new state each time a value changes. Power, current and voltage change on almost every read, so at this rate they add many rows to the database. Consider excluding the sensors you do not need from the recorder.

Raising the baud rate on the meter, and then here with Reconfigure, makes a poll quicker.

wrong_meter.description:
After the link to {title} came back, Home Assistant read the serial number of the meter at its address, and it is not the meter this entry was set up for. Its entities stay unavailable, so the other meter's readings do not end up in this meter's history.

If the meter was replaced, remove this entry and set up the new meter. If two meters share the address, give each its own address on the meter, then select **Reconfigure** on this entry. This message goes away once the right meter answers again.
